result.topic_en: The page finishes a derivation of a function $f b$ in terms of $\sin$, then begins the 'Pentagramma mirificum' (a self-polar spherical pentagram), with a figure and relations between the five sides and their differentials.
result.transcription:
Es ist folglich
$f b = \frac{\lambda}{\varrho} \sin \frac{\varrho k}{\lambda} . b$
$f(\xi - b) = \frac{\lambda}{\varrho} \cos \frac{\varrho k}{\lambda} . b$
$1 = \sin \frac{\varrho\varrho k}{\lambda}$
woraus $\frac{\varrho\varrho k}{\lambda} = \frac{1}{2}\pi$
also
$f b = \frac{\lambda}{\varrho} \sin \frac{\pi}{2\varrho} . b .$

Pentagramma mirificum
[figure: spherical pentagon with sides labelled 1–5 and outer dotted lines labelled R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5]

8 $-d1 = d2.\cos 4 + d5.\cos 3$
9 $-d2 = d3.\cos 5 + d1.\cos 4$
10 $-d3 = d4.\cos 1 + d2.\cos 5$
11 $-d4 = d5.\cos 2 + d3.\cos 1$
12 $-d5 = d1.\cos 3 + d4.\cos 2$
Die Elimination von $d5$ aus 8 und 11 gibt
$d1.\sin 3^2 = -d2.\cos 4 + d4.\cos 2 \cos 3$
Die Elimination von $d3$ aus 9 und 10 hingegen [?]
$d2 \sin 5^2 = -d1.\cos 4 + d4.\cos 1.\cos 5$

$\cos 1 = \sin 2.\sin 5$
$\cos 2 = \sin 3.\sin 1$
$\cos 3 = \sin 4.\sin 2$
$\cos 4 = \sin 5.\sin 3$
$\cos 5 = \sin 1.\sin 4$
$1 = \cos 1.\mathrm{tg} 3.\mathrm{tg} 4 = \cos 2 \mathrm{tg} 4.\mathrm{tg} 5$
$= \cos 3.\mathrm{tg} 5.\mathrm{tg} 1 = \cos 4 \mathrm{tg} 1.\mathrm{tg} 3$
$= \cos 5 \mathrm{tg} 2.\mathrm{tg} 4$

III 479

methods.what: Determination of the constant from the normalisation condition, giving a sine form for f
Differential relations among the five sides of the pentagramma mirificum
Elimination of differentials between the relations
Elimination of d3 from relations 9 and 10
Napier-type relations between the parts of the pentagramma mirificum: cosine of each side equals the product of sines of two others
Equivalent tangent relations for the pentagramma mirificum
